annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete local paper for the missing-tier audit, including both CGS algorithms and the full appendix proof, and compared all missing-tier candidates with the full frozen Mathlib and NumStability baselines; the existing T3 was retained.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P11 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

corpus_membership: This paper is part of the current corpus listed in metadata/manifest.json.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 105, issue 2, 2006, printed pages 299-313

rejected_candidates.candidate: Algorithm 1 (CGS-S), Algorithm 2 (CGS-P), and the floating-point model
rejected_candidates.reason: These are definitions and assumptions. The paper's contribution is the corrected analysis of CGS-P, not the pseudocode or IEEE model in isolation.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Lemma 1 quoted from Giraud et al.
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly states that this lemma is incorrect for Algorithm 1, so it cannot serve as a valid target.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 1 clauses (4)-(6) and (8) as standalone T3 targets
rejected_candidates.reason: These clauses support the selected numbered orthogonality result. T3 uses uniform forms of (4)-(6) while deriving equation (7), rather than replacing the selected conclusion with one supporting estimate.
The condition-number conversion relies on Weyl monotonicity, pseudoinverses, and O(epsilon squared) bookkeeping and is secondary to the corrected Gram-Schmidt result.
The MATLAB counterexamples and measured errors are empirical evidence, not finite proof targets.
This is a qualitative possibility outside Theorem 1's assumptions rather than a quantified finite result.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the CGS2 and CGS-K reorthogonalization discussion
rejected_candidates.reason: The section presents algorithmic implications, parameter choices, and heuristics; it does not prove a new self-contained finite theorem.
The local diagonal and projection bounds retain first-order O notation and mainly set up the appendix induction; the selected tasks capture the exact reusable core and main consequence.

These are long intermediate first-order bounds with paper-specific constants. The residual action in (16) is the clean direct tier, while the final defect identity and bound provide stronger higher-tier targets.

T1.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. No source theorem has exactly one substantial NumStability dependency: the nearby operator-action and conditioning steps are elementary, while the paper-specific CGS-P execution analysis has no corresponding library theorem.

T2.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. No CGS-P result matches two substantial frozen theorems. The reusable rectangular associativity, transpose, and norm facts are basic; the difficult loss-of-orthogonality and first-order execution analysis remains paper-specific.

T3.decision: Use numbered equation (7) for every positive prefix of one fixed-input family of linked rectangular CGS-P executions, preserving condition (3), spectral norms, c4(m,k), kappa2(R_k)^2, and a uniform interpretation of the source's O(epsilonM^2) remainder.

selection_policy: Use correct claims proved in this paper and retain their algorithm, dimensions, hypotheses, norms, constants, and quantifier scope.
Reject the explicitly incorrect cited lemma, experiments, heuristics, and definitions as standalone proof targets.
Represent each unspecified O(epsilon squared) term by coefficients and a radius fixed uniformly before selecting a positive machine unit.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after checking the mounted frozen object baseline, not broader source-only Gram-Schmidt modules.
